questions.question: If the radius of a cylindrical tank is 7 m and its height is 9 m, then find the capacity of the tank (in m³ ). (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The capacity of a cylindrical tank is equivalent to its volume.

Volume = Base Area × Height = πr²h

V = (22/7) × 7 × 7 × 9

V = 22 × 7 × 9 = 154 × 9 = 1386 m³

**∴ The correct answer is 1386 m³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the cylindrical tank (r) = 7 m

Height of the cylindrical tank (h) = 9 m

**Formula Used:**

Capacity of Cylinder (Volume) = πr²h

questions.question: The average pocket money of three children X, Y and Z of a family is ₹2,500 in a particular month. Y spends double and Z spends triple of what X spends during that month. If the average of their unspent money is ₹2,100, then X spends (in ₹):

Total pocket money = 3 × 2500 = ₹7,500

Total unspent money = 3 × 2100 = ₹6,300

Total spent money = 7500 − 6300 = ₹1,200

Ratio of spending (X : Y : Z) = 1 : 2 : 3 (Total 6 units)

Amount spent by X (1 unit) = 1200 ÷ 6 = ₹200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹200.**

**Formula Used:**

Total = Average × Number of entities

Total Money = Total Spent + Total Unspent

questions.question: Fifty-four men can complete a work in 48 days. After 8 days of working, thirty-six more men joined them. How many days will they now take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Remaining work for the initial 54 men is for 40 days (48 − 8).

Total men working now = 54 + 36 = 90 men.

Using the rule M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂ ⇒ 54 × 40 = 90 × D₂

D₂ = 2160 ÷ 90 = 24 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of men = 54

Total time to complete the work = 48 days

Additional men who joined after 8 days = 36

**Method Used:**

Total Work Method, assuming 1 man completes 1 unit of work per day.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 54 Men
 48
 2592
 54
 
 

⇒ Total Work = 54 × 48 = 2592 units

⇒ Work completed in 8 days = 54 × 8 = 432 units

⇒ Remaining Work = 2592 − 432 = 2160 units

⇒ Total men working after 8 days = 54 + 36 = 90 men

⇒ New combined efficiency = 90 units/day

⇒ Days required to complete remaining work = Remaining Work ÷ New Efficiency

⇒ Days required = 2160 ÷ 90 = 24 days

**∴ The correct answer is 24 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

MDH Rule

If M₁ men can do W₁ work in D₁ days working H₁ hours, and M₂ men can do W₂ work in D₂ days working H₂ hours, then: (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂.

Efficiency & Time Relationship

The efficiency of a group is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task. If efficiency increases, time required decreases proportionally.

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in direct proportion to the amount of work done by each individual. When individuals work for the same number of days, wages are shared in the ratio of their efficiencies.
</p

questions.question: The price of fuel decreases by 10%, 50% and 50% in three successive months, but increases by 45% in the fourth month. What is the percentage increase/decrease in the price of fuel in the fourth month as compared to its original price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the original price of the fuel be 100 units.

Successive multiplying factors are 0.9, 0.5, 0.5, and 1.45.

Final Price = 100 × 0.9 × 0.5 × 0.5 × 1.45 = 32.625

Total Decrease = 100 − 32.625 = 67.375%

Rounding to two decimal places, the percentage decrease is 67.38%.

**∴ The correct answer is Decreases by 67.38%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial price undergoes successive changes of −10%, −50%, −50%, and +45%.

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± R₁/100) × (1 ± R₂/100) × ...

Percentage Change = [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100

 Successive Percentage Changes

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial price of the fuel be 100 units.

⇒ Price after 1st month = 100 × (1 − 10/100) = 100 × 0.9 = 90

⇒ Price after 2ⁿd month = 90 × (1 − 50/100) = 90 × 0.5 = 45

⇒ Price after 3rd month = 45 × (1 − 50/100) = 45 × 0.5 = 22.5

⇒ Price after 4th month = 22.5 × (1 + 45/100) = 22.5 × 1.45 = 32.625

⇒ Overall decrease = Original Price − Final Price = 100 − 32.625 = 67.375 units

⇒ Percentage decrease = (67.375 ÷ 100) × 100 = 67.375%

⇒ Rounding to two decimal points, we get 67.38%.

**∴ The correct answer is Decreases by 67.38%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a quantity undergoes multiple consecutive percentage changes, the final value is evaluated by multiplying the base value by the respective successive multipliers: Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± r₁/100) × (1 ± r₂/100).

Effective Percentage Formula

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the net effective percentage change can be quickly calculated using the formula: Net % = (a + b + ab/100)%. Positive values indicate an increase, while negative values indicate a decrease.

Order Independence

The final resultant percentage in successive changes is completely independent of the sequence in which the changes are applied. For example, a 50% decrease followed by a 10% decrease yields the exact same final value as a 10% decrease followed by a 50% decrease.
</p

questions.question: Siddhant invested some money in HDFC at 4% per annum rate of interest. What would be the corresponding simple interest (in ₹) if after 2 years, Siddhant got ₹255 as compound interest, considering annual compounding?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective CI rate for 2 years = 4% + 4% + (4 × 4) ÷ 100% = 8.16%

Effective SI rate for 2 years = 4% × 2 = 8%

Given CI = ₹255 ⇒ 8.16% ≡ ₹255

Required SI = 8% ≡ (255 ÷ 8.16) × 8 = 25500 ÷ 102 = ₹250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate (R) = 4% p.a., Time (T) = 2 years, Compound Interest (CI) = ₹255

**Formula Used:**

CI = P[(1 + R ÷ 100)² − 1]

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ CI = P[(1 + 4 ÷ 100)² − 1] = 255

⇒ 255 = P[(26 ÷ 25)² − 1]

⇒ 255 = P[(676 ÷ 625) − 1]

⇒ 255 = P[51 ÷ 625]

⇒ P = (255 × 625) ÷ 51

⇒ P = 5 × 625 = ₹3125

⇒ Now, calculate Simple Interest for the same principal:

⇒ SI = (3125 × 4 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 25000 ÷ 100 = ₹250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio of CI and SI for 2 years

The ratio of Compound Interest to Simple Interest for two years at a rate R% per annum can be directly calculated as: CI ÷ SI = 1 + (R ÷ 200).

Effective Rate of Interest for 2 years

For a given rate R%, the effective CI rate for 2 years is: 2R + (R² ÷ 100)%. The effective SI rate is strictly 2R%.

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The exact difference between compound interest and simple interest for 2 years is given by the formula: D = P(R ÷ 100)².

questions.question: Which of the following numbers must be added to each of the numbers 9, 16, 13 and 23 so that the resulting numbers are in proportion?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a number 'x' is added to a, b, c, d to make them proportional: x = (bc − ad) ÷ [(a + d) − (b + c)]

Here a = 9, b = 16, c = 13, and d = 23.

⇒ x = (16 × 13 − 9 × 23) ÷ [(9 + 23) − (16 + 13)]

⇒ x = (208 − 207) ÷ (32 − 29) = 1/3

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The original numbers are 9, 16, 13, and 23.

**Formula Used:**

For four numbers a, b, c, and d to be in proportion, a : b :: c : d ⇒ a/b = c/d.

 
 9
 
 ,
 
 
 16
 
 and
 
 
 13
 
 ,
 
 
 23

 
 
 

 
 

 

 

 

 

 
 Add 'x' to each number

 
 9 + x
 
 :
 
 
 16 + x
 
 ::
 
 
 13 + x
 
 :
 
 
 23 + x
 
 Condition for Proportion: (9 + x) / (16 + x) = (13 + x) / (23 + x)

**Calculations:**

Let the required number to be added be x.

⇒ According to the given condition, (9 + x) : (16 + x) :: (13 + x) : (23 + x)

⇒ (9 + x) / (16 + x) = (13 + x) / (23 + x)

⇒ By cross-multiplying the terms, we get:

⇒ (9 + x)(23 + x) = (16 + x)(13 + x)

⇒ 207 + 9x + 23x + x² = 208 + 16x + 13x + x²

⇒ 207 + 32x = 208 + 29x

⇒ 32x − 29x = 208 − 207

⇒ 3x = 1

⇒ x = 1/3

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proportion Rule

When four numbers a, b, c, d are in proportion (a:b :: c:d), the product of extreme terms equals the product of mean terms: a × d = b × c.

Componendo and Dividendo

If a/b = c/d, then according to this theorem, (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d). This rule is widely used to simplify complex fraction and proportion equations quickly.

Continued Proportion

Three numbers a, b, c are said to be in continued proportion if a:b = b:c. In this sequence, b is known as the mean proportional, and b² = ac.
</p

questions.question: A man goes to Chennai from Hyderabad at a speed of 24km/hr and returns to Hyderabad at speed of 40km/hr, through same route. What is his average speed (in km/hr) of the entire journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the distance traveled is the same in both directions, the average speed is given directly by the formula:

Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 24 × 40) ÷ (24 + 40)

⇒ Average Speed = 1920 ÷ 64 = 30 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 30 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 Hyderabad
 Chennai
 
 
•

• 
 

 Speed = 24 km/hr
 
 
• 
 

 Speed = 40 km/hr

**Given:**

Speed from Hyderabad to Chennai (S₁) = 24 km/hr

Speed from Chennai to Hyderabad (S₂) = 40 km/hr

Let the one-way distance between the two cities be D km.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken for the forward journey (T₁) = D ÷ 24

⇒ Time taken for the return journey (T₂) = D ÷ 40

⇒ Total Time = (D ÷ 24) + (D ÷ 40)

⇒ Total Time = (5D + 3D) ÷ 120

⇒ Total Time = 8D ÷ 120 = D ÷ 15

⇒ Total Distance covered = D + D = 2D

⇒ Average Speed = 2D ÷ (D ÷ 15)

⇒ Average Speed = 2 × 15 = 30 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 30 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for 3 Equal Distances

If an object covers three equal parts of a journey at speeds x, y, and z, the average speed is calculated as (3 × x × y × z) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Average Speed with Different Distances

If an object travels variable distances d₁, d₂, d₃ taking corresponding times t₁, t₂, t₃, the Average Speed is strictly given by (d₁ + d₂ + d₃) ÷ (t₁ + t₂ + t₃).

Relative Speed Concept

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (x + y). When moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (x − y).
</p

questions.question: The marked price of a chair was ₹19,200. The shopkeeper was offering it for a discount of 20%, but on further bargaining agreed to offer a successive discount and finally sold the chair for ₹13,824. What was the second discount offered by the shopkeeper?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Price after the first 20% discount = 80% of ₹19,200 = ₹15,360

Value of the second discount offered = ₹15,360 − ₹13,824 = ₹1,536

Second discount % = (1536 ÷ 15360) × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹19,200

First Discount (D₁) = 20%

Final Selling Price (SP) = ₹13,824

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = (Discount Value ÷ Base Price) × 100

 
 
 

 
 

 
 ₹19,200
 Marked Price

 
 ₹15,360
 After 1st Discount

 
 ₹13,824
 Final SP

 

 − 20%

 

 − x%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 19200 × (100 − 20) ÷ 100

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 19200 × 0.8 = ₹15,360

⇒ Amount of second discount = Price after 1st discount − Final Selling Price

⇒ Amount of second discount = 15360 − 13824 = ₹1,536

⇒ Second discount % = (Amount of second discount ÷ Price after 1st discount) × 100

⇒ Second discount % = (1536 ÷ 15360) × 100

⇒ Second discount % = 1 ÷ 10 × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

The single equivalent discount for two successive discounts of a% and b% can be directly calculated as: (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Marked Price vs Cost Price

Marked Price (MP) is the maximum retail price set by the shopkeeper. Discounts are always calculated on the MP, whereas Profit or Loss is strictly calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

Direct Relationship

The ratio linking MP, CP, Profit%, and Discount% is given by: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

questions.question: When difference between compound and simple interest for three years is ₹155 at 10% interest per annum, the principal is ₹______

Effective CI for 3 years at 10% = 33.1%

questions.question: A, B, C and D, working separately, can do a piece of work in 5 days, 6 days, 8 days and 10 days, respectively. In how many days can A and B complete the work together, if they are assisted by C and D on alternate days, starting with C?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(5, 6, 8, 10) = 120 units.

Efficiencies: A = 24, B = 20, C = 15, D = 12 units/day.

Day 1 work (A + B + C) = 24 + 20 + 15 = 59 units.

Day 2 work (A + B + D) = 24 + 20 + 12 = 56 units.

Work done in 2 days = 59 + 56 = 115 units. Remaining work = 120 − 115 = 5 units.

Time for remaining 5 units by A, B, C = 5 ÷ 59 days. Total time = 2 ⁵/₅₉ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 ⁵/₅₉ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A, B, C, and D separately is 5, 6, 8, and 10 days respectively.

A and B are assisted by C and D on alternate days, starting with C.

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken

**Calculations:**

Let Total Work be the LCM of 5, 6, 8, and 10 = 120 units.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 5
 120
 24
 
 

 B
 6
 20
 
 

 C
 8
 15
 
 

 D
 10
 12
 
 

⇒ Total efficiency of A and B = 24 + 20 = 44 units/day.

⇒ Work done on Day 1 (A + B + C) = 44 + 15 = 59 units.

⇒ Work done on Day 2 (A + B + D) = 44 + 12 = 56 units.

⇒ Total work done in one 2-day cycle = 59 + 56 = 115 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 120 − 115 = 5 units.

⇒ On Day 3, A, B, and C will work together (combined efficiency = 59 units/day).

⇒ Time taken to complete the remaining 5 units = 5/59 days.

⇒ Total time taken = 2 days + 5/59 days = 2 ⁵/₅₉ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 ⁵/₅₉ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Method for Time & Work

Total work is assumed as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given individual times. Efficiency of a person = Total Work ÷ Time taken.

Alternate Days Work

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the total work completed in one full cycle before analyzing the remaining work for the subsequent days.

Pipes & Cisterns

Follows the exact same logic as Time & Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency, while outlet pipes (leaks) have negative efficiency.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the direct ratio of the total amount of work actually done by each person, which is proportional to their efficiencies if they work for an equal duration.
</p

questions.question: An article is bought for Rs. 5,000 and sold for Rs. 6,200. Find the profit percentage.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Cost Price to Selling Price = 5000 : 6200 = 25 : 31

Profit in ratio = 31 − 25 = 6 units

Profit % = (6 ÷ 25) × 100 = 24%

**∴ The correct answer is 24%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 5,000

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 6,200

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
 CP = ₹5,000
 
 
 ₹1,200

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 SP = ₹6,200

**Calculation:**

⇒ Profit = 6200 − 5000

⇒ Profit = 1200

⇒ Profit % = (1200 ÷ 5000) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (12 ÷ 50) × 100

questions.question: When 12, 15, 18, 20 and 25 divide the least number x, the remainder in each case was 5 but x was divisible by 7. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The problem states that the required least number x must be perfectly divisible by 7.

We can efficiently find the correct answer by checking the given options for divisibility by 7.

Checking options: 3506 ÷ 7 (No) | 3560 ÷ 7 (No) | 3065 ÷ 7 (No).

Only 3605 ÷ 7 = 515, which yields a remainder of 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 3605.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = 12, 15, 18, 20 and 25

Remainder in each case = 5

The least number x is perfectly divisible by 7.

**Formula Used:**

Required Number = (LCM of divisors) × k + Remainder

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, we find the LCM of the given divisors: 12, 15, 18, 20 and 25.

⇒ 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ 15 = 3 × 5

⇒ 18 = 2 × 3²

⇒ 20 = 2² × 5

⇒ 25 = 5²

⇒ LCM = 2² × 3² × 5² = 4 × 9 × 25 = 900

⇒ Let the required number be x = 900k + 5, where k is a positive integer.

⇒ Since x is divisible by 7, the expression (900k + 5) must be a multiple of 7.

⇒ We can split 900k as (896k + 4k). Here, 896 is a multiple of 7, since 896 = 7 × 128.

⇒ Therefore, the divisibility depends entirely on (4k + 5) ÷ 7 leaving a remainder of 0.

⇒ Let's check for minimum integer values of k:

⇒ For k = 1: 4(1) + 5 = 9 (Not divisible by 7)

⇒ For k = 2: 4(2) + 5 = 13 (Not divisible by 7)

⇒ For k = 3: 4(3) + 5 = 17 (Not divisible by 7)

⇒ For k = 4: 4(4) + 5 = 21 (Perfectly divisible by 7)

⇒ Substitute k = 4 into the original equation x = 900k + 5.

⇒ x = 900 × 4 + 5 = 3600 + 5 = 3605.

**∴ The correct answer is 3605.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and Constant Remainders

When a number is divided by a, b, and c leaving the same remainder R in each case, the general form of the required number is represented as: N = k × LCM(a, b, c) + R.

LCM and Different Remainders

When a number is divided by a, b, and c leaving remainders x, y, and z respectively, such that the difference (a − x) = (b − y) = (c − z) = K, the general form of the number is: N = k × LCM(a, b, c) − K.

Divisibility Rule of 7

To check if a number is divisible by 7, drop the last digit, double it, and subtract it from the remaining truncated number. If the result is exactly divisible by 7 (or is 0), then the original number is also divisible by 7.
</p

questions.question: The LCM of 16, 21, 364 and 156 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Start with the largest number: 364 = 2² × 7 × 13.

Compare with 156 (2² × 3 × 13) → the factor 3 is missing in 364, so multiply by 3 → 364 × 3 = 1092.

Compare with 21 (3 × 7) → both factors 3 and 7 are already present in 1092.

Compare with 16 (2⁴) → 1092 only contains 2², so we must multiply by the remaining 2² (which is 4).

LCM = 1092 × 4 = 4368.

**∴ The correct answer is 4368.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers = 16, 21, 364, and 156

**Concept Used:**

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors of the given numbers.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 16 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 2⁴

⇒ Prime factorization of 21 = 3 × 7 = 3¹ × 7¹

⇒ Prime factorization of 364 = 2 × 2 × 7 × 13 = 2² × 7¹ × 13¹

⇒ Prime factorization of 156 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 13 = 2² × 3¹ × 13¹

⇒ The prime factors present across all numbers are 2, 3, 7, and 13.

⇒ Highest power of 2 = 2⁴

⇒ Highest power of 3 = 3¹

⇒ Highest power of 7 = 7¹

⇒ Highest power of 13 = 13¹

⇒ LCM = 2⁴ × 3¹ × 7¹ × 13¹

⇒ LCM = 16 × 3 × 7 × 13

⇒ LCM = 48 × 91

⇒ LCM = 4368

**∴ The correct answer is 4368.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

It is the greatest number that divides exactly into two or more given numbers. It is obtained by multiplying the lowest powers of all common prime factors.

Relation between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers 'a' and 'b': HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b. (Note: This rule is valid only for two numbers).

LCM of Fractions

LCM of fractions = (LCM of all numerators) ÷ (HCF of all denominators).

HCF of Fractions

HCF of fractions = (HCF of all numerators) ÷ (LCM of all denominators).
</p

questions.question: Two trains having lengths of 410 m and 390 m are running at speeds of 80 km/h and 100 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance to cross = 410 + 390 = 800 m

Relative speed (same direction) = 100 − 80 = 20 km/h

Speed in m/min = 20 × (1000 ÷ 60) = 1000/3 m/min

Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 800 × (3 ÷ 1000) = 2.4 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 2.4 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Length of first train (L₁) = 410 m

Relative Speed

When two bodies travel in the same direction, their relative speed is calculated by taking the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). If they travel in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Train Crossing Distance

questions.question: 400 mangoes were bought at ₹1220 per hundred and were sold at a profit of ₹820. Find the selling price (in ₹) per dozen of mangoes.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price of 1 mango = 1220 ÷ 100 = ₹12.2

Profit on 1 mango = 820 ÷ 400 = ₹2.05

Selling Price of 1 mango = 12.2 + 2.05 = ₹14.25

Selling Price per dozen (12 mangoes) = 14.25 × 12 = ₹171

**∴ The correct answer is ₹171.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of mangoes bought = 400

Cost of 100 mangoes = ₹1220

Total profit on selling all mangoes = ₹820

1 dozen = 12 mangoes

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price = Cost Price + Profit

 
 
 
 Total CP = ₹4880
 Profit = ₹820

 Total SP = ₹5700

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Cost Price (CP) of 400 mangoes = (1220 ÷ 100) × 400 = ₹4880

⇒ Total Selling Price (SP) of 400 mangoes = Total CP + Total Profit

⇒ Total SP = 4880 + 820 = ₹5700

⇒ Selling Price of 1 mango = 5700 ÷ 400 = ₹14.25

⇒ Selling Price of 1 dozen mangoes = 14.25 × 12 = ₹171

**∴ The correct answer is ₹171.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when the Selling Price (SP) is greater than the Cost Price (CP). The actual profit amount is calculated as: Profit = SP − CP.

Profit Percentage

Profit percentage is calculated on the base of Cost Price unless stated otherwise. Formula: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Unitary Method

It is an essential technique in arithmetic where the value of a single unit is found first, which is then multiplied to find the value of the required number of units (like finding the cost of 1 dozen from 1 piece).
